title: "References"
description: "Works the joshpy documentation draws on, grouped by tutorial"
---

joshpy implements no statistics of its own. Optimization and inference come from
established packages maintained by others, and the tutorials describe them in
the terms of the papers below. Each tutorial lists the works it cites at the end
of its page. This page collects them, grouped by tutorial.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Adding a reference

Add the BibTeX entry to `docs/references.bib`, cite it in a page with `[@key]`,
and list it below under that page's heading. Quarto formats the citation and
adds the entry to the page's own reference list.
:::

## Simulation-Based Inference with ABC

[Tutorial](tutorials/sbi-abc.qmd)

- @hartig2011: the framework the tutorial follows for stochastic ecological
  simulation models: aggregation into summary statistics, likelihood
  approximation, and sampling.
- @cranmer2020: the wider field of simulation-based inference, including
  amortized neural estimators and calibrating an inference procedure.
- @toni2009 and @beaumont2009: sequential Monte Carlo ABC and its importance
  weights, as implemented in sbi.
- @boelts2025: the sbi package that `SbiStrategy` runs.
- @beaumont2002: scaling summary statistics, and regression adjustment of
  accepted parameters.
- @wood2010: synthetic likelihood, a parametric likelihood approximation.
- @wilkinson2013: the tolerance read as an explicit model-error term.
- @grimm2005: pattern-oriented modelling, whose patterns are summary statistics.
- @beven2006: equifinality.
- @talts2018: simulation-based calibration.
- @csillery2012: leave-one-out cross-validation of rejection ABC on a stored set
  of simulations.
- @malchow2024: comparing prior and posterior to show what fitting an
  individual-based model learned from monitoring data.

## Adaptive Parameter Optimization

[Tutorial](tutorials/adaptive-sweep.qmd)

- @akiba2019: Optuna, the framework behind `OptunaStrategy`.
- @bergstra2011: the tree-structured Parzen estimator (TPE), the sampler the
  tutorial uses.
